sec: PBC laboratory, histopathology, treatment; PSC definition, prevalence, HLA, presentation, UC association, labs

items.q: Laboratory features of PBC — match the marker with its printed positivity — 1) AMA (Type IgM) 2) ANA … A) +ve in 50% B) +ve in 95%
items.exp: Laboratory features: Raised ALP; AMA (Type IgM) +ve in 95%; ANA +ve in 50%. (Book p1021)

items.q: Fill up: The first laboratory feature listed for PBC is raised ______, and the AMA is printed as being of the ______ isotype.
Which histopathological feature is labelled the EARLIEST change in PBC?
opts: Loss of the canal of Hering
Florid duct lesion with non-caseating granulomas
items.exp: Histopathology tree: 'Loss of the canal of Hering : Earliest'. (Book p1021)

items.q: Which histopathological feature of PBC is labelled most common (m/c)?
opts: Loss of the canal of Hering

items.q: Judge: I The most characteristic histological lesion of PBC is the florid duct lesion with granulomas. II These granulomas are caseating.
items.exp: 'Florid duct lesion with granulomas (Non-caseating) (most characteristic)'. (Book p1021)

items.q: Match the PBC treatments with the printed descriptor — 1) Ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) 2) Obeticholic acid … A) Farnesoid receptor agonist B) ↓ progression of biliary cirrhosis
items.exp: Treatment: UDCA : ↓ progression of biliary cirrhosis; Obeticholic acid : Farnesoid receptor agonist. (Book p1021)

items.q: Fill up (PSC definition): Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis is progressive ______ destruction of intra and extra hepatic bile duct, and is an ______ disease due to leaky gut.
items.exp: 'Progressive fibrosing destruction of intra and extra hepatic bile duct. IgG4 disease d/t leaky gut.' (Book p1021)

items.q: Prevalence of PSC: sex predilection and decade printed?
Which HLA associations are printed for PSC?
Which item is NOT among the four PSC presentation bullets on this page?
items.exp: Presentation: Fatigue, Pruritis, Leaky gut, Cholestasis. (Book p1021)

items.q: Which cancer is printed under 'Association with cancer' for PSC?
items.exp: 'Association with cancer : Cholangiocarcinoma.' (Colorectal carcinoma appears separately under the UC association.) (Book p1021)

items.q: Interpret the printed figures for the PSC–ulcerative colitis association: '(2/3rd / 5%)'.
opts: 2/3rd of PSC cases have UC; 5% of UC cases have PSC
2/3rd of UC cases have PSC; 5% of PSC cases have UC
2/3rd of PSC cases develop colorectal carcinoma; 5% die
Both figures refer to the lifetime cholangiocarcinoma risk
items.exp: 'Ulcerative colitis (2/3rd / 5%) (2/3rd cases of PSC have UC & 5% cases of UC have PSC).' (Book p1021)

items.q: Regarding the UC that accompanies PSC, judge: I It is associated with atypical p-ANCA. II Its type is pancolitis with rectal sparing. III The only treatment is transplant.
opts: I, II and III all true
I and II true, III false
I true, II and III false
II true, I and III false
items.exp: Sub-bullets under UC: Atypical P. ANCA association; Type: pancolitis with rectal sparing; A/w colorectal carcinoma; Only treatment: transplant. (Book p1021)

items.q: Fill up: The UC associated with PSC is 'A/w ______ carcinoma'.
Laboratory features of PSC — which of the following is printed as NEGATIVE?
opts: Both IgG4 and p-ANCA are printed negative
items.exp: Laboratory features: IgG4 antibody; Atypical P. ANCA Ab; 'AMA Ab : −ve'. (Book p1021)
